Ghana’s Electric Utilities Workers Launch Strike, Disrupting Power Distribution

Accra, June 18—Workers across Ghana’s electric utilities sector launched a strike Tuesday morning, halting routine operations and prompting significant disruptions in the country’s electricity distribution network. The action, organized by the National Union of Electricity Workers, centers on grievances over delayed salary payments and concerns about outdated safety equipment.

Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd, the country’s largest power distributor, confirmed that the walkout has affected its ability to maintain and restore service. In a statement released midday, the firm said, “Ongoing industrial action by essential staff has led to delays in addressing faults and responding to customer complaints. We urge customers to bear with us as we seek a resolution.”

According to the union, over 4,000 employees in Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi, and other major cities have joined the walkout. Key functions impacted include emergency repairs, technical support, and meter installations. Local media reported that several regional offices of Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd and the privately operated Voltic Power Services have closed their doors to the public for the duration of the strike.

“This is not a decision we take lightly,” said Kofi Mensah, chairman of the National Union of Electricity Workers, speaking outside the main Electricity Co Of Ghana Ltd headquarters in Accra. “After months of negotiations, workers are frustrated by unfulfilled promises on wage arrears and the failure to provide adequate safety gear. Our members are committed to ensuring safe, reliable power, but we cannot do so under current conditions.”

Analysts estimate that the strike could further strain an already pressured sector. “Even a one- or two-day stoppage will lead to a backlog of maintenance, with possible knock-on effects for reliability,” said Ama Ofori, an energy sector analyst at West African Markets Research. She noted that the walkout comes at a time of high demand due to seasonal heat.

While no immediate nationwide outages have been reported, several neighborhoods in Accra and Kumasi have experienced prolonged power interruptions. The Ghana Grid Management Authority said it is monitoring the situation and working with management teams to implement contingency measures.

Negotiations between union representatives and management were ongoing at the time of writing, with both sides expressing hope for a swift resolution.
